name: 둥근 지붕 돌 처마 띠(천장 줄 1칸, 벽면 바로 위) (dome cornice)
label: atlas_biome_interior/plus/dome cornice
reasons: 화풍: 윤곽이 근흑(재질 어두운 톤 아님) (4/4)

surfaces.part: cornice strip (highlight, mid band, dark shadow)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 16-wide rectangle on every row (0-15). Rows 0-10 are a flat brick wall face with mortar lines. Row 11 is a light 1-row highlight. Rows 12-13 are a mid-tone band and rows 14-15 are dark. This reads as a front-facing cornice strip with a highlight and shadow, not a horizontal top plane. No band sits above a front-edge line, no ellipse is present, and no roof plane or visible contents are drawn. The piece is a flat wall-mounted face, so it reads as a front elevation with no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a grey brick-course band with about 4 lightness steps (dark mortar/outline, mid grey, light grey, a faint highlight). The references use about 5-6 steps. Its dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral black/grey line, not a tinted dark material tone. The well-roofed (33% neutral), hedge (0%) and cheese-stall (1%) references all lean toward the colour of the adjacent material. The candidate has 8 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge and 17-20 for the stall and well. That is the low end, and it falls well short of the richer references. It has no flat fills (0% near-flat), and the bricks are individually shaded, but with little per-brick grain or highlight variation. It reads as a clean but somewhat sticker-like outlined block, shallower than the Beodeul references.

surfaces.part: cornice band (highlight line, face strip, dark lower strip)

answer.evidence: Rows 0-10 are a face-on brick pattern with mortar lines at rows 3 and 7, so they form a vertical wall face. Row 11 is a 1-row light highlight (L=113). Rows 12-13 are a mid-tone strip and rows 14-15 are dark. This reads as a front-facing molding strip with a highlight, not a sloped top plane. The width is 16 on every row, so there is no ellipse and no receding top or side. At most the row-11 highlight is a 1-row rim, so there is no real top surface. As a wall-mounted piece it is acceptable to draw flat, and it matches the 'front elevation' and 'rim only' reference cases.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small grey stone brick cornice strip, about 1 tile. It shows roughly 3 grey steps: light brick faces, a mid tone and a dark mortar/outline. The measured 8 visible tones per tile are close to the hedge (9) but well below the well (20) and cheese stall (17). The dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline and mortar read as a neutral dark grey/black line, not a tint of the stone. That is the sticker-like look the Beodeul references avoid, since the hedge is 0% and the stall 1%. There is no near-flat coverage, but the bricks look like flat rectangles with little per-stone grain or highlights, and the 'dome' roundness is barely modelled. Compared with the references' 5-6 steps and tinted edges, it is shallower and flatter.

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 16-wide rectangle on every row, so there is no ellipse or widening. Rows 0-10 are a brick wall face with mortar lines at rows 3 and 7, which is a vertical face. Row 11 is a 1-row lighter line (L=113), and rows 12-13 are a mid-tone band (L=84). Rows 14-15 are dark (L=37). Together these read as a front-facing cornice strip: a 1-row highlight, then a band, then shadow below it. That is a rim and not a top surface, because no band of rows sits above a front-edge line to show a horizontal plane receding. There is no roof or awning plane and no contents. The drawing is a flat wall-mounted front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small grey stone-brick cornice strip with a neutral near-black outline. 100% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, versus 0-1% for the hedge and cheese stall and 33-44% for the well and bench, so it reads as the 'sticker' outline rather than a dark material tone. The stone is shaded in only about 3 grey steps: bricks of one grey with dark mortar lines and little per-stone highlight. It has 8 visible tones per tile, below the hedge (9), stall (17) and well (20). There are no flat fills (0% near-flat), but the grain is sparse. The well's stones are shaded one by one with tinted outlines and the candidate is plainly shallower. It is also grey and neutral, but I did not judge hue; the problem is the structure of the outline and the shallow shading.

answer.evidence: Rows 0-10 are a flat brick wall face with mortar lines. Row 11 is a 1-row light highlight, rows 12-13 are a mid-tone strip, and rows 14-15 are dark. This reads as a front-facing cornice strip with a bevel highlight and a shadow below it. The strip does not end in a front-edge line followed by eave shadow, and it has no widening or narrowing ellipse. The silhouette is a constant 16 px wide for all rows. No horizontal top surface is visible, so this is a wall-mounted front elevation, which is allowed to be flat.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small grey stone band with a brick-like pattern. It has about 8 visible tones per tile, which is near the hedge reference (9) but well below the well (20) and stall (17). By eye, the stone body uses only about 3 lightness steps: a light grey face, a mid grey and a dark joint line. The bricks are separated mostly by dark lines rather than shaded one by one. All of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral (100%), so the outline is a colourless black/grey line, which gives the 'sticker' look. The well and hedge references have tinted outlines (33% and 0% neutral) with 5-6 steps per material. The candidate has no flat fills (0% near-flat) and some brick texture, but its shading is shallow and its outline is neutral, so it falls short of the Beodeul bar. It does not read as a rounded dome cornice with a lit curved face and a shadowed underside; it reads as a flat brick strip.
